title: Apache Tomcat Flaw Lets Attackers Bypass Security Constraints on WebSocket Endpoints
content_md: The Apache Software Foundation has released Apache Tomcat 11.0.26, fixing 12 vulnerabilities across WebSocket, HTTP/2, AJP, authentication, and TLS certificate-validation components . The release is particularly urgent for internet-facing deployments because it includes an Important-rated flaw that can allow attackers to bypass security constraints on WebSocket endpoints. Disclosed publicly on September 23, the issues affect a broad range of Tomcat 11 versions, with most extending from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.25. Apache does not issue binary patches for individual flaws, making an upgrade to Tomcat 11.0.26 the primary remediation path. Apache Tomcat Flaw The most significant issue, tracked as CVE-2026-76183, arises from Tomcat incorrectly parsing request paths as WebSocket endpoint templates. This behavior can enable a bypass of security constraints applied to WebSocket endpoints, potentially allowing an unauthorized user to reach services that application developers expected to be access-controlled. The update also fixes CVE-2026-87022, a WebSocket message-smuggling flaw affecting deployments that enable the per-message-deflate compression extension. Improper handling of a length parameter could allow an attacker to smuggle WebSocket messages, creating parsing inconsistencies between components handling the same connection.
